type: the contiguous object span [first object, last constructed object] that the loader instantiates
structure: Objects live only inside the enumerated span; embedded children are built by their owner

location.offset: section 1, first object (block end +0x1C) to the last record before the header table area

meaning: Three boots pin the enumeration: (1) a clone appended AFTER the last object stays raw and the level is fine; (2) a clone inserted BEFORE the tail objects is constructed; (3) redirecting a table entry to an unconstructed record hangs the post-construction table pass. So construction walks a contiguous span of records (not the header table, not a size stream, not ownership pointers from roots), each top-level record building the children embedded after it. To duplicate an entity the copy must land inside the span (igz clone-entity --insert-before) AND its embedded child must construct without error; the current clone hangs while building the child, which is the remaining M3 blocking unknown (candidate causes: a resource handle/flagged 0x8xxxxxxx field the child constructor dereferences, or a count/pointer inside the physics record that must be re-pointed, not just rebased).

evidence.summary: append-after-last: clone raw, level alive (132 heap copies of the spawn position)
insert-before-tail: clone owner constructed, embedded physics raw, load hung

confirmed: clone owner constructed as a 0x2A8 blob (= owner 0x94 + physics 0x214), the loader walked to the next table-listed record; the type-92 record owns a contiguous blob including its embedded tfbPhysicsModel
